newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end mixed in selective trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end mixed in selective trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly lower on Wednesday in selective trading, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares lost 0.19 percent, or 0.55 points, to 282.32 on all-share turnover of 180 million shekels against 266 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.09 percent lower at 289.51.

"Trading was mixed and selective today. The indices closed slightly lower because of profit taking, which is only normal in a market that made such a big move," said Gidi Halperin, investment manger at Meitav Investments and Securities.

Michael Politzer of Central Securites Corp said the session opened with mild losses in the Mishtanim of 0.7 percent but by midday the index recouped most of its losses, closing only slightly lower. "This shows how strong the market is. It simply does not want to fall," he said.
"New money keeps coming into the market, bond yields are declining and inflation expectations are at the lowest in a long time," Halperin said. "All this makes investment in stocks more attractive."
He said that from a technical point of view the market should stabilise before the Maof reaches 300.
Traders noted that investors focused on small-cap stocks traded on the Karam index.
Bank Hapoalim fell 1.0 percent to 783 agorot. Sahar Securities and Investments raised its 1997 earnings per share estimate for Bank Hapoalim to 0.85 shekels from a previous estimate of 0.73.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which lost 0.25 percent to 539 agorot on volume of 15.6 million shekels; Israel Discount Bank, which fell 1.0 percent to 370 agorot on turnover of 5.9 million shekels; and Israel Chemicals, which gained 0.5 percent to 427 agorot on volume of four million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
